html:
Seru Epenisa Cakobau was the warlord of the small island of Bau who became the most powerful chief in Fiji and, in 1871, its king. In 1874 he ceded the islands to Britain.

He became a Methodist in 1854, which helped him win the wars between Fijian confederacies with the backing of Tonga. But debts claimed by the United States, settler unrest and quarrels with rival chiefs left his kingdom bankrupt.

He chose British rule over collapse, and signed the Deed of Cession at Levuka in 1874. His war club was given to Queen Victoria and later returned as the mace of Fiji's parliament. His descendants remained leading chiefs. See also Great Council of Chiefs.
